item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Color of Caps

[Image: A pie chart indicating 30% white caps, 25% green caps, 15% black caps, 10% blue caps, and 20% red caps.]

The pie chart shows the percentage of caps for sale at a sporting goods store. If there are 200 caps, what is the total number of caps that are either white or green?
item.figure_description: A pie chart titled "Color of Caps" divided into five sectors: White (labeled "White 30%") occupying the top-left sector; Green (labeled "Green 25%") occupying the top-right quadrant; Red (labeled "Red 20%") occupying the bottom-right sector; Blue (labeled "Blue 10%") occupying a narrow sector at the bottom; and Black (labeled "Black 15%") occupying the sector between Blue and White on the lower left.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Sophie has a bag in which there are 16 marbles: 8 are red and 8 are black marbles. She draws 2 marbles from the bag and does not put them back. Both marbles are black. She then draws a third marble out of the bag. What can you say about the likely color of this third marble?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to be red than black.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to be black than red.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to be red or black.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot tell if red or black is more likely.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The total cost of the journey for all the students must be 500 zeds or less.
There are 30 students in the class.

Here are the costs for visiting each town:

| Visiting Acton or Camford | Visiting Burley or Darley |
| --- | --- |
| Student Rate | Student Rate |
| Round-trip ticket: 25 zeds | Round-trip ticket: 20 zeds |
| 1/3 off for groups of 25 or more students | 10% off for groups of 15 or more students |

Which towns can they afford to visit? Show your work.

descriptors: Show costs of 500 zeds for Acton and Camford; 540 zeds for Burley and Darley; Indicates Acton and Camford
Shows 500 zeds for Acton and Camford; 540 zeds for Burley and Darley; does not indicate Acton and Camford
Finds correct cost for visiting Acton and Camford (500 zeds) or Burley and Darley (540 zeds) but not both
Indicates Acton and Camford but no calculations or incorrect calculations shown
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Four students watched the traffic passing their school for 1 hour.

The table shows what they saw:

| Type of Vehicle | Number |
| :--- | :---: |
| Cars | 60 |
| Bicycles | 30 |
| Buses | 10 |
| Trucks | 20 |

Each student drew a graph to show the results. Which graph shows the results correctly?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four graphical representations of the traffic data:
- Option A: A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars correspond to: Cars = 60 (solid black bar), Bicycles = 30 (light gray bar), Buses = 10 (medium gray bar), Trucks = 20 (white bar with black border).
- Option B: A pictograph with a legend stating '1 wheel = 10 vehicles'. Cars has 5 wheels, Bicycles has 4 wheels, Buses has 1 wheel, and Trucks has 2 wheels.
- Option C: A vertical bar graph with the same axis and colors as Option A, showing: Cars = 60, Bicycles = 30, Buses = 20, Trucks = 10.
- Option D: A pie chart divided into four sectors: Cars covers the right half (180°, solid black). Bicycles covers the bottom-left quadrant (90°, light gray). The remaining top-left quadrant is divided between Buses (a larger sector, medium gray) and Trucks (a smaller sector, white).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).
